category: Raw Signal Analysis · Firtina Lab, UMD
title: RawMod: A Deep Learning Approach to Modification-Agnostic Classification in Nanopore Sequencing
organization: Nanopore raw signal · DNA modification detection · Anomaly detection
summary: A modification-agnostic classifier that detects DNA modifications directly from raw nanopore signal, without requiring a control sample.
overview: RawMod piles up raw signal from up to 30 reads at a candidate site, refines each read against a reference k-mer lookup table, and passes the pileup through a convolutional trunk feeding a transformer that attends across reads to reach a consensus modification likelihood.
highlights: Anomaly detection model architecture for modification agnostic classification.
Won the Best Poster Award at HiTSeq, ISMB 2026.

title: Deep Learning for Complex Structural Variation in Cancer Genomes
organization: Long-read WGS · Somatic variation · Cancer genomics
summary: Developing a ML framework that combines copy-number and breakpoint-graph representations to detect BFB, chromothripsis, ecDNA, and seismic amplification.
overview: Our tool generates label-free candidate regions, embeds copy-number and breakpoint-graph evidence with pretrained encoders, and supports both semi-localized event detection and multilabel chromosome-level screening.
highlights: Built a label-free, multi-evidence candidate generator for complex genomic regions.
Pretrained copy-number and breakpoint-graph encoders and fused their representations for downstream classification.
Developed localized MIL and chromosome-level multilabel models with genome-held-out evaluation.

category: Short Read Copy Number Variation · Fritz Lab, UMD
title: Pesticide Resistance in Helicoverpa zea
organization: Structural bioinformatics · Copy number variation · Population genomics
summary: Exploring causes of Bt pesticide resistance in H. zea. Then, exploring the applications of these insights in future genomic monitoring.
overview: This work includes population genomics, understanding protein-protein interactions between resistance genes and the Bt toxin, and benchmarking short read CNV tools on insect trios.
highlights: Benchmarking five CNV detection methods against H. zea trios that are internally sequenced.
Built structural models of the duplicated trypsin protein docking onto the Cry toxin receptor complex to reason about the resistance mechanism.
Presented at PAG 2026; recipient of 2nd Prize in the CSSA Poster Competition.

title: Host–Pathogen Coevolution ODE Model
organization: Temporal adaptation · Allelic variation · Seasonal forcing
summary: A deterministic ODE system for asking when hosts and pathogens should adapt over time under allelic variation, seasonal forcing, and birth pulses.
overview: The model represents host–pathogen coevolution with seasonal dynamics and competing pathogen genotypes. It produces testable predictions about pathogen timing for future laboratory and field experiments.
highlights: Model temporal adaptation and allelic variation.
Represent seasonal forcing and birth pulses.
Presented at the EEID NE 2025 Poster session and QEED Seminar.

category: Computer Vision · Gemstone Team FSH, UMD
title: Social Behavior Classification in Lake Malawi Cichlids
organization: Computer vision · Few-shot deep learning · Action localization · PI: Abhinav Shrivastava
summary: A few-shot classification framework for identifying social behaviors of Lake Malawi cichlids from video, where fish look similar and behavior labels are expensive.
overview: I lead a team of 11 students and serve as the main point of contact between our team and PI Abhinav Shrivastava. This project is an interdisciplinary effort between labs working in Computer Vision and Genetics, inspiring my interests in multimodal work between the two fields.
highlights: Develop few-shot behavior classification from video.
Build a per-fish instance segmentation and keypoint tracking pipeline to turn raw tank footage into structured trajectories.
